shin-splints.title: Possible shin splints
shin-splints.description: Irritation along the inner edge of the shin from repeated foot strikes.
shin-splints.advice: Skip painful runs and reduce your training load before building up gradually.

stress-fracture.title: Possible stress fracture
stress-fracture.description: A small bone injury from repeated stress can cause pain in one spot that gets worse with impact.
stress-fracture.advice: Stop running and have this pain checked before returning to impact exercise.

it-band.title: Possible IT band syndrome
it-band.description: Irritation of the band along the outside of the thigh, felt on the outside of the knee while running.
it-band.advice: Reduce long runs and avoid downhill runs or sloping ground that bring on the pain.

kneecap.title: Possible runner's knee
kneecap.description: Pain around or behind the kneecap when the knee works repeatedly.
kneecap.advice: Avoid painful exercise, then gradually build up running time and downhill runs.

patellar.title: Possible patellar tendinopathy
patellar.description: Irritation of the tendon between the bottom of the kneecap and the shin.
patellar.advice: Reduce painful fast runs, jumps and hills before gradually increasing the load again.

quadriceps-tendon.title: Possible quadriceps tendinopathy
quadriceps-tendon.description: An injury to the quadriceps tendon where it attaches just above the kneecap.
quadriceps-tendon.advice: Avoid painful knee bends under load and downhill runs. Gradually adjust how much the tendon works.

pes-anserine.title: Possible pes anserine bursitis
pes-anserine.description: Irritation of a small fluid-filled sac below the inner knee, near the tendon attachments.
pes-anserine.advice: Reduce hills and runs that bring on the pain.

meniscus.title: Possible meniscus injury
meniscus.description: An injury to the cartilage inside the knee can cause joint pain and a catching feeling after a twist.
meniscus.advice: Avoid painful turns and impact exercise. Have the injury checked if the catching continues.

baker.title: Possible Baker's cyst
baker.description: A pocket of fluid behind the knee can cause a lump and tightness when bending.
baker.advice: Reduce painful movements and have a lump checked if you do not know what caused it.

elongation.title: Possible mild muscle strain
elongation.description: A pulling feeling in one area without a clear loss of strength may be a mild muscle injury.
elongation.advice: Avoid painful exercise, sprints and forced stretching. Build up gradually when normal movements feel comfortable.

muscle-tear.title: Possible muscle tear
muscle-tear.description: Sudden muscle pain that forces you to stop may be a muscle tear.
muscle-tear.advice: Stop running and have the injury checked before returning. Do not test it by sprinting.

muscle-soreness.title: Likely muscle soreness
muscle-soreness.description: Muscle pain that starts after a harder session and eases with rest.
muscle-soreness.advice: Leave more rest between hard sessions and return gradually as the pain eases.

adductor-tendon.title: Possible adductor tendinopathy
adductor-tendon.description: Pain where the inner thigh muscles attach near the groin, brought on by running and long strides.
adductor-tendon.advice: Avoid painful bursts of speed and forced stretching before gradually building up the load again.

outer-hip.title: Possible gluteal tendinopathy
outer-hip.description: Tendon pain on the side of the hip, made worse by repeated steps or pressure.
outer-hip.advice: Reduce painful runs and avoid lying on the sore side.

proximal-hamstring.title: Possible upper hamstring tendinopathy
proximal-hamstring.description: Irritation where the hamstrings attach just below the buttock.
proximal-hamstring.advice: Avoid painful long strides and fast sessions. Limit sitting positions that press on the sore area.

achilles.title: Possible Achilles tendinopathy
achilles.description: Pain in the tendon from the calf to the heel, often after rest or when pushing off.
achilles.advice: Reduce painful hills and fast runs, then gradually build up the load on the tendon.

achilles-rupture.title: Possible Achilles tendon rupture
achilles-rupture.description: Sudden pain followed by a loss of push-off strength may mean the tendon has torn.
achilles-rupture.advice: Do not run again. Have the tendon checked promptly without testing its strength.

anterior-tibial.title: Possible tibialis anterior tendinopathy
anterior-tibial.description: Pain at the front of the ankle along the muscle and tendon that lift and lower the foot.
anterior-tibial.advice: Avoid long downhill runs and painful movements that lift the foot.

compartment.title: Possible exertional compartment syndrome
compartment.description: Muscle pressure that returns at a similar level of effort and eases when you stop may suggest this condition.
compartment.advice: Avoid exercise that brings on the pressure. Have it checked if it keeps returning.

tibial-tendon.title: Possible posterior tibial tendinopathy
tibial-tendon.description: Pain along the inner ankle towards the arch when putting weight on the foot.
tibial-tendon.advice: Reduce painful steps and long runs. Wear shoes that feel comfortable and stable.

peroneal-tendon.title: Possible peroneal tendinopathy
peroneal-tendon.description: Pain in the tendons behind the outer ankle bone, often made worse by uneven ground.
peroneal-tendon.advice: Avoid uneven trails and sloping ground that bring on the pain for now.

sprain.title: Possible ankle sprain
sprain.description: A twist can injure the ligaments around the ankle. This questionnaire cannot rule out a fracture.
sprain.advice: Protect the ankle and avoid painful steps. Have it checked if walking is difficult or the pain gets worse.

plantar.title: Possible plantar fasciitis
plantar.description: Irritation of the band of tissue under the foot, between the heel and the toes.
plantar.advice: Reduce long periods of painful standing or walking. Wear comfortable shoes before returning gradually.

heel-pad.title: Possible heel pad syndrome
heel-pad.description: Irritation of the tissue that cushions foot strikes under the centre of the heel.
heel-pad.advice: Avoid painful impact and hard ground without enough cushioning.

metatarsalgia.title: Possible metatarsalgia
metatarsalgia.description: Pain under the front of the foot, just before the toes, when putting weight on it.
metatarsalgia.advice: Reduce strong push-offs and painful runs. Check that your shoes do not squeeze the front of your foot.

morton.title: Possible Morton's neuroma
morton.description: An irritated nerve between the toes can cause burning or a feeling like a small stone in the shoe.
morton.advice: Reduce pressure on the front of the foot and exercise that brings on the pain.

extensor-tendon.title: Possible foot extensor tendinopathy
extensor-tendon.description: Pain along the tendons on top of the foot that lift the toes.
extensor-tendon.advice: Avoid tight laces and painful movements. Do not run just to test the area.

unclear.title: The answers do not point to one injury
unclear.description: The answers do not clearly separate the possible injuries in this area.
unclear.advice: Edit your answers to describe the exact spot and what the pain feels like.
